fi-pomacanthus-imperator.title: Emperor Angelfish
fi-pomacanthus-imperator.summary: A large angel; adults are blue with yellow stripes, a dark eye mask and a yellow-orange tail. The catalog SKU is a changing (sub-adult) fish.
rows: About 1' 3 in; wild record 40 cm (15.7 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
With caution. Large angels nip corals and clams
Omnivore. Algae and spirulina-based foods plus meaty foods; graze on live rock
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Line and Tuamoto islands, North to southern Japan and the Ogasawara Islands, South to the Great Barrier Reef, New Caledonia
notes: Needs a 220 gal or larger tank with live rock for grazing and hiding.

fi-apolemichthys-trimaculatus.title: Flagfin Angelfish
fi-apolemichthys-trimaculatus.summary: A shy angel that is hard to keep because its natural diet is largely sponges.
rows: About 10 in; wild record 26 cm (10.2 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep as the only angel in the tank
No. Nips soft and stony corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Needs sponge-based angelfish foods; adapts poorly to other foods
Indo-West Pacific: East Africa south to 28°S and east to Samoa, north to southern Japan, south to Australia
notes: Shy at first; needs lots of hiding places in a 125 gal or larger tank.

fi-pygoplites-diacanthus.title: Regal Angelfish
fi-pygoplites-diacanthus.summary: A prized angel rated expert-only; how well it adapts depends a lot on where it was collected.
rows: About 10 in; wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
With caution. May nip corals and clams
Omnivore. Needs sponge-based angelfish foods plus a varied meaty and algae diet
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to Ryukyu and Ogasawara islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia
notes: Fish from the Red Sea, Maldives, Coral Sea, Fiji and Tahiti are said to ship and adapt better than other Indo-Pacific fish.

fi-pomacanthus-semicirculatus.title: Koran Angelfish
fi-pomacanthus-semicirculatus.summary: A popular, hardy large angel (also called the Semicircle Angelfish). This SKU is a juvenile.
rows: About 15 in; wild record 40 cm (15.7 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
No. Nips stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Grazes slime algae and cyanobacteria on live rock; feed algae and meaty foods
Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Samoa, north to southern Japan, south to Western Australia and New South Wales, including Lord Howe Island
notes: Grows big; 250 gal or more is recommended.

fi-pomacanthus-paru.title: French Angelfish
fi-pomacanthus-paru.summary: A large Atlantic angel; the gill cover has a yellow rim. This SKU is a juvenile, and it grows big.
rows: About 15 in; wild record 41.1 cm (16.2 in) TL (FishBase)
No. Nips corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, sponge-based angelfish foods and mysis or frozen shrimp
Western Atlantic: Florida, USA and Bahamas to Brazil, including the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean
notes: Needs 250 gal or more with lots of live rock.
warn: Tends to dominate the tank as it grows.

fi-holacanthus-tricolor.title: Rock Beauty Angelfish
fi-holacanthus-tricolor.summary: A striking black-and-yellow angelfish from the tropical western Atlantic. In the wild it feeds mainly on sponges, which makes it a hard fish to keep long term.
rows: About 12 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 35 cm (13.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore that feeds mainly on sponges in the wild: offer sponge-based angelfish foods as the core of the diet, with grazing on live rock
Western Atlantic: Georgia (USA), Bermuda, and northern Gulf of Mexico to Santa Catarina, Brazil
notes: Needs angelfish foods that contain sponge plus constant grazing on mature live rock; not for beginners.
Easily stressed despite being semi-aggressive; young fish may pick at the slime coat of slow tankmates.
